mainTopic: Intent about the skin of the tail and whether it makes a קרבן פיגול, plus the Torah source for why intent outside the time brings כרת but intent outside the place does not.
overview: The גמרא asks how intent to eat the skin of the tail late can make a קרבן פיגול, since the tail is burned on the מזבח, not eaten. שמואל answers that our משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who counts switched intent, even though the next משנה follows the חכמים. רב הונא instead says the skin is not like the tail, so it is eaten. רב חסדא says the skin is like the tail, but the משנה is talking about a young goat's tail, which is eaten. The גמרא explains why each אמורא did not take the others' approach. It then brings a ברייתא about an עולה that seems to fit רב הונא and challenge רב חסדא, and רב חסדא gives two answers. Next the גמרא asks for the source that intent outside the place only disqualifies, while intent outside the time is פיגול with כרת. רבה reads one פסוק, but his reading gets stuck, so אביי begins a new approach from two separate פסוקים, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The skin under the tail counts like the tail
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier answer: the skin under the tail is treated as part of the tail (אליה).
steps.simpleTranslation: It is considered like the tail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it started before this section. It says the skin under the tail is treated as part of the tail itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the skin is counted as tail, it follows the tail's rules. That matters because the tail of a sheep שלמים is burned on the מזבח, not eaten. This sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The fatty tail of a sheep, which is burned on the מזבח
Is considered like, is similar to

phrases.english: It is considered like the tail;
phrases.notes: He means the skin under the tail, which the גמרא was talking about just before this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends an answer given just before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Classification: the skin is counted as part of the tail.
steps.terutzMaskana: The skin under the tail follows the rules of the אליה.

steps.title: But that intent moves the tail from the altar to a person
steps.stepSummary: If the skin counts as tail, it belongs on the מזבח. So intending to eat it means switching it from the altar to a person, which normally does not make a קרבן פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is intending to move it from being eaten by the altar to being eaten by a person!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks what it just said. If the skin is like the tail, the person's plan to eat it is a plan to switch it from the מזבח to a human.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally פיגול only happens when you have wrong-time intent about something in its normal role: eating what is normally eaten, or burning what is normally burned. Here the tail is meant for burning, but he plans to eat it. So why should the משנה call it פיגול?

keyTerms.meaning: Has a thought or intent (מחשבה) while doing the עבודה
Literally the altar's eating, meaning burning on the מזבח
A קרבן ruined by intent to eat or burn it after its proper time

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'eating by the altar' does not mean eating. It is a way of saying the part is burned on the מזבח.

phrases.english: But he is intending
to move it from consumption by the altar to a person!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the result of step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that this intent makes the קרבן פיגול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Switched intent, from altar to person, should not create פיגול, yet the משנה says it does.

steps.title: שמואל: The משנה follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that our משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who holds that intent switching a part between the altar and a person does count.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי אליעזר, who says that a person's intent works even if he shifts something from the altar's eating to a person's eating, or from a person's eating to the altar's eating.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the challenge. He says the משנה is following one specific תנא, רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that intent works in both directions: altar to person, and person to altar. So for him, planning to eat the tail late can still make the קרבן פיגול. The question goes away, but only if the משנה is רבי אליעזר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
Intent can be applied, and it counts
Eating by a person

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Eliezer's;
who says: one can have intent
from consumption by the altar to consumption by a person,
and from consumption by a person to consumption by the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הָא מַנִּי – רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: the משנה follows one specific תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the משנה follows the usual rule that switched intent does not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי אליעזר, for whom switched intent does count.

steps.title: The source for רבי אליעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה showing that רבי אליעזר disagrees with the חכמים about intent toward something not normally eaten or burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If someone slaughters the קרבן intending to eat something that is not normally eaten, or to burn something that is not normally burned, the קרבן is fit. But רבי אליעזר says it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where we know רבי אליעזר's opinion from. It quotes a משנה where he argues with the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say intent only counts for a part's normal role, so this קרבן stays fit. רבי אליעזר says even an unusual intent counts, so he makes the קרבן unfit. This backs up שמואל's description of רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Its normal way or use
To burn on the מזבח
Makes it unfit

phrases.english: As we learned: One who slaughters the offering
to eat an item that is not normally eaten;
to burn an item that is not normally burned –
it is fit. And Rabbi Eliezer deems it unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַזֶּבַח לֶאֱכוֹל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין דַּרְכּוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the view שמואל used in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר counts intent about a part outside its normal role.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on דף ל״ה, where the חכמים say כשר and רבי אליעזר says פוסל.
steps.whatToRemember: חכמים: intent only counts for a part's normal role (eating what is eaten, burning what is burned). רבי אליעזר: even switched intent counts.

steps.title: But the next משנה sounds like it is not רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל by quoting the next משנה's general rule, which requires intent about a part's normal role. That sounds like the חכמים, not רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain our משנה? As רבי אליעזר? Then look at the next part: This is the rule: anyone who slaughters, receives the blood, carries it, or throws it, intending to eat something that is normally eaten, or to burn something that is normally burned...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge to שמואל. It quotes the כלל from the next משנה, and step 6 finishes the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כלל speaks only of eating what is normally eaten and burning what is normally burned. That matches the חכמים, who say switched intent does not count. If the same משנה continues with the חכמים' view, how can the earlier part follow רבי אליעזר?

keyTerms.meaning: How did you explain it? Which view did you put it with?
Look at the later part of the משנה
This is the general rule
Receiving the blood, carrying it, throwing it, three of the four main עבודות

phrases.english: How did you explain it – as Rabbi Eliezer?
Say the later part: This is the rule:
Anyone who slaughters, or who receives the blood,
or who carries it, or who throws it;
intending to eat an item that is normally eaten,
or to burn an item that is normally burned.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי אוֹקֵימְתַּהּ – כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר? אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that our משנה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כלל in the next part only counts intent about a part's normal role, which sounds like the חכמים, so the משנה does not seem to be רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: The next rule matches the חכמים, so the משנה would be split
steps.stepSummary: The general rule in the next משנה only counts intent about something normally eaten. That is the view of the חכמים. So the first clause would follow רבי אליעזר and the later clause would follow the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule says: something normally eaten makes the offering פיגול, and something not normally eaten does not. That is the view of the Rabbis. So is the first clause רבי אליעזר and the later clause the Rabbis?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it started in Step 5. It points out that שמואל's reading would split one משנה between two opposing views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'only what is normally eaten' fits the חכמים, who say intent about something outside its normal role does not count. If שמואל is right that the first clause follows רבי אליעזר, the משנה would switch opinions partway through. That is an awkward way to read a משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה or ברייתא
The later clause
Its normal way or normal use
We have arrived at (the view of...)

phrases.english: An item that is normally eaten: yes,
phrases.notes: He means: intent to eat it at the wrong time does make the offering פיגול.

phrases.english: one that is not normally eaten: no;
we have arrived at the Rabbis.
The first clause is Rabbi Eliezer
and the latter clause is the Rabbis?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge that began in Step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that the משנה follows רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The next clause clearly follows the חכמים, so שמואל's reading forces a split משנה.

steps.title: שמואל accepts the split משנה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers simply: yes, the first clause follows רבי אליעזר and the later clause follows the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל does not back down. He agrees that the משנה switches opinions between clauses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rather than looking for a new reading, שמואל accepts the awkward result. For him, a משנה can follow two different opinions in two clauses.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.
phrases.notes: שמואל is the one answering here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6 by accepting it
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the challenged result (a split משנה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A split משנה should be impossible, so שמואל must be wrong
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל holds that the רישא is רבי אליעזר and the סיפא is רבנן

steps.title: רב הונא: the skin is not counted as the tail
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the skin under the tail is not like the tail. So it is not burned on the מזבח; it is eaten. Then the whole משנה can follow the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The skin of the tail is not considered like the tail.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא gives a different approach. He rejects the starting idea from Step 1 that the skin counts as part of the tail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the skin is not part of the tail, it is not burned on the מזבח and is simply eaten. So intent to eat it is about its normal role, and it makes the offering פיגול even according to the חכמים. Both clauses of the משנה can then follow the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: The skin of the fat tail
Is not considered like...

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The skin of the tail is not considered like the tail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the challenge in Step 2, avoiding שמואל's split משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the skin is a separate part, not tail
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The skin counts as tail and belongs on the מזבח
steps.terutzMaskana: The skin is eaten, so the משנה follows the חכמים throughout

steps.title: רבא gives the פסוק behind רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains רב הונא's reason from the פסוק 'its fat, the tail': the fat of the tail goes on the מזבח, but not the skin of the tail.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is רב הונא's reason? 'Its fat, the tail', and not the skin of the tail.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא supports רב הונא with a פסוק. He shows where the idea that the skin is separate from the tail comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names the fat of the tail as what is offered. רבא reads this as limiting: the fat goes on the מזבח, the skin does not. So the skin is treated as ordinary eaten meat.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
'Its fat, the tail' (from the פסוק)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַב הוּנָא?
phrases.english: Rava said: What is the reason of Rav Huna?
"Its fat, the tail"
and not the skin of the tail.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רב הונא's ruling
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's claim that the skin is not like the tail
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'חלבו האליה', read as excluding the skin

steps.title: רב חסדא: the משנה is talking about a young goat's tail
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא agrees the skin is like the tail. But he says the משנה is about the tail of a young goat, which is not burned on the מזבח and is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Really, the skin of the tail is like the tail. But here we are dealing with the tail of a young goat.
steps.whatsHappening: A third approach. רב חסדא keeps the rule that the skin counts as tail, but says the משנה is talking about a different animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a sheep's tail is burned on the מזבח. A goat's tail is eaten, and so is its skin. So intent to eat it is about its normal role, and the whole משנה follows the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / in truth (keeping the original rule)
Here, what case are we dealing with?
A young goat

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא is not saying the skin is separate from the tail. He agrees it counts as tail. He changes the animal, not the rule about the skin.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Really, the skin of the tail is considered like the tail;
and here, what are we dealing with?
With the tail of a young goat.
phrases.notes: A goat's tail isn't put on the מזבח; it gets eaten, so intent to eat it is normal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further alternative answer to Step 2, different from both שמואל and רב הונא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a specific animal (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about a sheep's tail, which goes on the מזבח
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a goat's tail, which is eaten, so it follows the חכמים

steps.title: Why each אמורא rejected the other approaches
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רב חסדא did not follow שמואל because they did not want to split the משנה. שמואל and רב חסדא did not follow רב הונא because they held that the skin of the tail is like the tail.
steps.simpleTranslation: None of them said like שמואל, because they did not want to set the first clause as רבי אליעזר and the later clause as the Rabbis. They did not say like רב הונא, because they understood that the skin of the tail is like the tail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up the three approaches. It explains what made each אמורא avoid the others' answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate issues. First, can a משנה be split between two views? רב הונא and רב חסדא say no. Second, is the skin part of the tail? שמואל and רב חסדא say yes. רב חסדא's goat-tail answer is the one that keeps both: no split, and the skin counts as tail.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them
They set / interpret (a source as following a certain view)
They understood (literally: it is heard by them)

steps.whatToRemember: Three readings of the משנה: שמואל splits it (רבי אליעזר, then חכמים). רב הונא says the skin is not tail, so it is eaten. רב חסדא says the skin is tail, but the case is a goat's tail, which is eaten.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the גמרא's usual preference: avoid reading one משנה as two opposing views when another reasonable reading exists.

phrases.english: All of them do not say like Shmuel
phrases.notes: "All of them" here means רב הונא and רב חסדא.

phrases.aramaic: רֵישָׁא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְסֵיפָא רַבָּנַן לָא מוֹקְמִי.
phrases.english: because they do not set the first clause as Rabbi Eliezer and the latter clause as the Rabbis.
They do not say like Rav Huna
phrases.notes: This part is about שמואל and רב חסדא.

phrases.aramaic: עוֹר אַלְיָה כְּאַלְיָה דָּמֵי קָא מַשְׁמַע לְהוּ.
phrases.english: because they understood that the skin of the tail is considered like the tail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the three approaches and explains why each was chosen
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The disagreement depends on two questions: whether a משנה may be split, and whether the skin of the tail counts as tail.

steps.title: Why not explain the משנה like רב חסדא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל and רב הונא did not follow רב חסדא. Their reason is that his reading makes the משנה teach something already taught in חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why don't they say like רב חסדא? Because then what would the משנה be teaching us, that the skin of the tail is like the tail? We already learned that in another משנה: 'These are the ones whose skins are like their meat: the skin under the tail.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues explaining why each אמורא did not follow the others. Now it asks why שמואל and רב הונא did not explain the משנה the way רב חסדא did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב חסדא, the משנה's new point is only that the skin of the tail counts like the tail itself. But a משנה in חולין already lists the skin under the tail as skin that counts like meat. So רב חסדא's reading seems to make our משנה repeat a known rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
What is it teaching us? This asks what new point a source adds.
The skin of the fat tail of a sheep

phrases.aramaic: כְּרַב חִסְדָּא – מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמְרִי?
phrases.english: Like רב חסדא, what is the reason they do not say?
What would it be teaching us?
That the skin of the tail is like the tail?!
We already learned: 'And these are the ones whose skins are like their meat:'
the skin under the tail!

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַב חִסְדָּא – מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the survey from step 11 of why each אמורא did not take the others' approach
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's explanation of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His reading leaves the משנה teaching only a rule that a משנה in חולין already teaches.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the lesson was needed for קדשים
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the חולין rule is only about impurity. For קדשים we might have thought the skin does not count, because כהנים eat their portions the way kings eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא says it was needed. You might have thought the rule in חולין applies only to impurity, where the soft skin joins together with the meat. But here, with קדשים, the פסוק says 'for a consecrated portion,' meaning for greatness, the way kings eat. Kings do not usually eat this skin, so I might say it does not count. The משנה teaches us that it does.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא defends his reading. He shows that our משנה teaches something the משנה in חולין does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in חולין treats the skin like meat only for impurity, because soft skin joins together with the meat to make up a measure. For קדשים there is an extra factor: the כהנים' portions are eaten in a 'royal' way, and kings do not eat tail skin. So without our משנה we might have said the skin does not count as part of the tail for קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary to teach this.
It would have entered your mind to say this. It introduces a mistaken first thought.
Ritual impurity
Joins together with the meat to make up a measure
'For a consecrated portion.' Here it is read as 'for greatness,' eaten like royalty.

steps.whatToRemember: Each אמורא has a reason for not following the others. רב חסדא's reading is not a repeat, because קדשים have a special 'royal eating' factor that impurity laws do not have.

phrases.english: And רב חסדא says: it was needed;
it would enter your mind to say:
this applies only to the matter of impurity,
because it is soft, it joins together with the meat.
But here I would say: 'for a consecrated portion'
means for greatness, the way kings eat;
and kings do not usually eat this,
so I would say it does not count;
so the משנה teaches us that it does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the teaching is needed, by separating impurity laws from קדשים laws
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Tail skin might not count for קדשים, since kings do not eat it and כהנים eat their portions like royalty.
steps.terutzMaskana: The skin of the tail counts like the tail even for קדשים.

steps.title: A ברייתא about intending to burn the skin under the tail
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. It says that slaughtering an עולה while intending to burn the skin under the tail at the wrong place or time affects the offering, so this skin is treated as something burned on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: One who slaughters an עולה intending to burn an olive-sized piece of the skin under the tail. If he intends to burn it outside its place, the offering is פסול, but there is no כרת. If he intends to burn it after its time, it is פיגול, and one is liable to כרת for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as a challenge. It treats the skin under the tail as a part that gets burned on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wrong intent about burning a part matters only if that part really goes on the מזבח. The ברייתא picks an עולה, where everything is burned anyway, including the skin. Step 16 uses that choice of an עולה to challenge רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: To burn on the מזבח
Outside its proper place
After its proper time
An offering ruined by intent to eat or burn it after its time
The punishment of being cut off

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not say anyone actually burned the skin. It is only about his intent while slaughtering. That intent matters only if the skin is a part that is supposed to go on the מזבח.

phrases.english: They challenged: one who slaughters an עולה
intending to burn an olive's size of the skin under the tail;

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ – פָּסוּל, וְאֵין בּוֹ כָּרֵת;
phrases.english: if outside its place, it is פסול, but there is no כרת;

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ – פִּיגּוּל, וְחַיָּיבִין עָלָיו כָּרֵת.
phrases.english: if after its time, it is פיגול, and one is liable to כרת for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge after the survey of approaches ends
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's view that the skin of the tail always counts like the tail, in every offering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא limits the case to an עולה. That suggests the skin under the tail is burned only in an עולה and not in other offerings, which fits רב הונא but not רב חסדא. Step 16 spells this out.

steps.title: The ברייתא's second opinion: all skins that count like meat
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with a view in the name of רבי יעקב and רבי שמעון. The same laws of wrong intent apply to every skin listed as 'like its meat,' including the skin under the tail.
steps.simpleTranslation: אלעזר בן יהודה of Avelim says in the name of רבי יעקב, and רבי שמעון בן יהודה of Kefar Ikos said the same in the name of רבי שמעון: The skin of the hooves of small animals, the skin of the head of a young calf, the skin under the tail, and every skin the חכמים listed for impurity as 'these are the ones whose skins are like their meat' (which includes the skin of the private area): if outside its place, it is פסול with no כרת; if after its time, it is פיגול, and one is liable to כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second opinion. It applies the same intent rules to a whole list of skins that count like meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opinion also names the skin under the tail, and it adds the full list of skins that count like meat in the impurity laws. Wrong intent about any of these skins affects the offering. The ברייתא is still talking about an עולה, which is the detail the challenge in step 16 is built on.

keyTerms.meaning: Small animals such as sheep and goats
The area of the hooves
A young, tender calf
The private area of the animal

phrases.english: אלעזר בן יהודה, a man of Avelim,
says in the name of רבי יעקב,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אִישׁ כְּפַר עִיכּוּס
phrases.english: and so too רבי שמעון בן יהודה, a man of Kefar Ikos,
would say in the name of רבי שמעון:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד עוֹר בֵּית הַפְּרָסוֹת בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה,
phrases.english: Whether the skin of the hooves of small animals,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד עוֹר הָרֹאשׁ שֶׁל עֵגֶל הָרַךְ,
phrases.english: or the skin of the head of a young calf,
or the skin under the tail,
or any that the חכמים listed regarding impurity
under 'these are the ones whose skins are like their meat',
which includes the skin of the private area;

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ – פָּסוּל, וְאֵין בּוֹ כָּרֵת;
phrases.english: if outside its place, it is פסול, but there is no כרת;

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ – פִּיגּוּל, וְחַיָּיבִין עָלָיו כָּרֵת.
phrases.english: if after its time, it is פיגול, and one is liable to כרת for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן יְהוּדָה אִישׁ אֲבֵלִים אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא that was quoted as a challenge in step 14
steps.raayaObject: That the skin under the tail is treated like meat and like the tail for the laws of intent in קדשים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second opinion in the ברייתא, in the name of רבי יעקב and רבי שמעון

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא mention only a burnt offering?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא speaks only of an עולה. That fits רב הונא, but it is hard for רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Only a burnt offering, yes, but not another offering. Granted, according to רב הונא, that is why it says 'burnt offering.' But according to רב חסדא, why does it specifically say 'burnt offering'? Let it say 'offering'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא closely. It notices that it says only 'עולה' and uses this to challenge רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא holds that the skin of the tail is not like the tail in other offerings. So it makes sense that the ברייתא picks an עולה, where everything is burned anyway. רב חסדא holds the skin always counts like the tail, so the ברייתא should have said any offering (זבח).

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
Any animal offering (here: offerings other than an עולה)
Granted / it makes sense according to
Why specifically this case?

phrases.english: A burnt offering, yes, but another offering, no.
Granted, according to Rav Huna,
that is why it teaches 'a burnt offering.'
But according to Rav Chisda,
why does it specifically teach 'a burnt offering'?
Let it teach 'an offering'!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב הוּנָא הַיְינוּ דְקָתָנֵי עוֹלָה אֶלָּא לְרַב חִסְדָּא מַאי אִירְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a close reading from the ברייתא quoted in steps 14-15
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's view that the skin of the tail always counts like the tail
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule applies to every offering, the ברייתא should not have limited itself to an עולה.

steps.title: רב חסדא's two answers: a kid's tail, or change the wording
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the ברייתא speaks of a goat's tail, or that the wording should be changed to 'זבח'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא could say to you: If you want, say it is about the tail of a kid. And if you want, say: read it as 'offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא defends his view with two different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First answer: the ברייתא is talking about a young goat. A goat's tail is burned only in an עולה, so the ברייתא had to say עולה. Second answer: change the wording of the ברייתא to say 'זבח', so it covers every offering.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say (introduces an answer, often one of two)
The fat tail of a sheep
A young goat (kid)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's mention of עולה does not disprove רב חסדא. It may be about a kid, or the text should read 'זבח'.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda could say to you:
If you wish, say it is about the tail of a kid;
phrases.notes: A goat's tail is not burned in other offerings, only in an עולה, where the whole animal goes on the מזבח.

phrases.english: and if you wish, say: teach 'an offering.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב חִסְדָּא אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two options: narrow the case to a kid's tail, or change the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word עולה seemed to show that only an עולה is meant, against רב חסדא
steps.terutzMaskana: The word עולה is either needed for a goat's tail, or the text really says זבח

steps.title: Where do we learn the place-versus-time difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and asks for the source of its rule: intent outside the proper place only disqualifies, with no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'It is disqualified and there is no כרת,' etc. From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה and asks for the source in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that intent to eat or sprinkle outside the proper place makes the offering פסול but brings no כרת. Intent outside the proper time makes it פיגול, which does bring כרת. The גמרא wants to know which verses teach this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Disqualified
Spiritual cutting off, a severe punishment
From where are these things learned?

phrases.english: It is disqualified and there is no כרת in it, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה. Intent outside the place only disqualifies; intent outside the time makes it פיגול, with כרת.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse that teaches the difference between intent outside the place and intent outside the time

steps.title: שמואל: two verses are written
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that two separate verses are written, one for each kind of intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Two verses are written.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a short answer to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because there are two separate phrases in the Torah, the two kinds of wrong intent are treated differently. Only one of them is called פיגול with כרת. Steps 21-22 give רבה's explanation of which phrases these are. That explanation runs into trouble, and step 26 starts אביי's new explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Two verses or phrases
Are written

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
Two verses are written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 18
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference comes from two separate written verses

steps.title: Which verses does שמואל mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which two verses שמואל is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are they?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for details about שמואל's short answer. This sets up רבה's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל did not name the verses. The גמרא wants to know exactly which words he meant.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (asks for the details)

phrases.english: What are they?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of step 19
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the two verses

steps.title: רבה: 'third' refers to intent outside its time
steps.stepSummary: רבה begins explaining. The word 'third' in the verse refers to intent to eat after the proper time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: 'Third' is about intent outside its time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה starts to explain שמואל. He shows that the first phrase, 'on the third day,' is about intent outside the proper time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about eating שלמים on the third day is read as speaking about intent outside the time, and that is the case of פיגול. This is the first of the two phrases. The second phrase, for intent outside the place, comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Third (the third day)
Outside its proper time

phrases.english: Rabba said:
'Third' — this is outside its time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה שְׁלִישִׁי זֶהוּ חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'third' in ויקרא 7:18 refers to intent outside its time

steps.title: רבה finishes: 'פגול' means place, and 'ממנו' limits כרת to time
steps.stepSummary: רבה finishes reading the פסוק. 'פגול' refers to intent to eat outside the proper place. 'והנפש האוכלת ממנו' teaches that only one kind of intent brings כרת: intent to eat after the proper time, and not intent to eat outside the proper place.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'It shall be פגול' refers to intent to eat outside its proper place. 'And the soul that eats of it' means one, not two. That one is intent to eat after its proper time, which leaves out intent to eat outside its proper place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה continues explaining the פסוק. He shows which word teaches about intent outside the proper place, and which words limit כרת to intent after the proper time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21, 'שלישי' was tied to intent after the proper time. Now 'פגול' is tied to intent outside the proper place, so the פסוק teaches both kinds of intent. The word 'ממנו' ('of it', in the singular) is read as 'only one of them brings כרת', and רבה says that one is intent after the proper time.

keyTerms.meaning: A קרבן ruined by improper intent during its service
Intent to eat the קרבן outside its proper area
Intent to eat the קרבן after its proper time
One, and not two: only one of the cases is included
To exclude

phrases.english: 'Piggul': this is intent outside its proper place.
phrases.notes: Both this word and the next quote come from the same פסוק, ויקרא 7:18.

phrases.english: 'And the soul that eats of it' (shall bear its sin):
one and not two;
phrases.notes: The word 'of it' is singular, so only one of the two kinds of intent gets כרת.

phrases.english: this is intent beyond its proper time,
and to exclude intent outside its proper place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבה's explanation that began in step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'שלישי' teaches time, 'פגול' teaches place, and 'ממנו' limits כרת to time alone

steps.title: Why not reverse it and give כרת to place?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה. Maybe 'והנפש האוכלת ממנו' gives כרת to intent outside the proper place and leaves out intent after the proper time.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: 'And the soul that eats of it' refers to intent outside its place, which leaves out intent beyond its time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבה chose time for כרת. The same words could just as easily point to place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ממנו' only tells us that one of the two gets כרת. It does not say which one. So רבה's choice looks unjustified unless some reason picks out time.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead (opens a challenge suggesting the opposite reading)

phrases.english: But say: 'And the soul that eats of it':
this is intent outside its proper place,
and to exclude intent beyond its proper time!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's choice of which intent gets כרת
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's reading that 'ממנו' gives כרת to time
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'ממנו' only means 'one of the two', so the reverse reading fits the words equally well

steps.title: Time is preferred because the verse opens with it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that time makes more sense for כרת, because the פסוק begins with it ('the third day').
steps.simpleTranslation: It stands to reason that intent beyond its time is preferable, since the verse opened with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה. Time gets כרת because it is mentioned first in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק begins with 'ביום השלישי', which is time, and only later says 'פגול', which is place. The argument is that the first thing mentioned is the main subject, so the כרת clause goes back to it.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason
Is preferable, the better choice
Because the verse opened with it

phrases.english: It stands to reason that beyond its time is preferable,
since it opened with it.
phrases.notes: The פסוק starts with 'on the third day', which is about time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical preference based on word order
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either kind of intent could be the one with כרת
steps.terutzMaskana: Time wins because the פסוק opens with it

steps.title: On the contrary: place sits right next to the כרת clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that answer. Place should be preferred, because 'פגול' comes right before 'והנפש האוכלת ממנו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! Intent outside its place is preferable, since it is right next to it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back with an opposite argument of equal strength. This leaves רבה's reading without solid support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being mentioned first (time) is matched against being right next to the כרת words (place). Neither argument clearly wins, so the reading of 'ממנו' stays undecided. This is what sets up אביי's new approach in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
Because it is adjacent to it

phrases.english: On the contrary! Outside its place is preferable,
since it is adjacent to it!
phrases.notes: The word 'פגול' comes right before 'and the soul that eats of it' in the פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 24
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The 'opened with it' argument, and with it רבה's whole reading
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Being next to the כרת clause is just as strong a reason as being mentioned first

steps.title: אביי starts a new approach based on a ברייתא about an extra 'third'
steps.stepSummary: אביי sets רבה aside. He reports in the name of רב יצחק בר אבדימי that שמואל was relying on a ברייתא. That ברייתא notes that 'שלישי' in פרשת קדושים seems extra, because ויקרא פרק ז already says it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: When רב יצחק בר אבדימי came, [he said in the name of רב] that he relied on what the תנא taught. When the Torah says 'third' in the portion 'You shall be holy', there was no need to say it, since it was already said: 'And if any of the flesh of the peace offering be eaten on the third day'.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a new explanation of which two פסוקים שמואל meant. He begins by quoting a ברייתא that points out an extra-looking פסוק, which sets up a new way to learn the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's approach of reading one פסוק two ways got stuck. So אביי looks at two different פסוקים, one in פרק ז and one in פרק יט, both about eating on the third day. Because the second mention seems unnecessary, it must be teaching something new, and the explanation continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the previous approach)
He relied on what the תנא taught
The Torah portion beginning 'You shall be holy' (ויקרא פרק יט)
There is no need for the verse to say it (it seems extra)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different פסוקים about eating on the third day: ויקרא 7:18 and ויקרא 19:7. The ברייתא is asking why the second one is needed.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי [אָמַר רַב],
phrases.english: When Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi came, [he said that Rav said],
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording. Some versions don't have them.

phrases.english: he relied on what the tanna taught:
When it says 'third'
in the portion of 'You shall be holy',
for there is no need for the verse to say it,
since it was already stated:
'And if any of the flesh of the peace offering be eaten at all
on the third day';

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבה's reading, which stalled in steps 23-25, with a new answer to the question of step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two פסוקים are ויקרא 7:18 and ויקרא 19:7. The extra 'שלישי' in פרשת קדושים is the basis of the teaching, which continues on the next amud.
